summary.headline: Ambuja FY26 volumes hit a record 73.7 Mt (+16%), but Q4 cost ran ~INR4,500/t and management reset FY27 guidance to ~80 Mt with capacity targets pushed out.
summary.overview: FY26 was a record volume year for Ambuja, with 73.7 million tonnes sold (up 16% YoY) and normalized EBITDA of INR6,539 crore (up 31%, INR887/t). Q4 cost per tonne was about INR4,500, above the INR4,000 exit target, driven by acquired-asset underperformance (Sanghi 57%, Penna 46% utilization), freight, packing, fuel, branding and repairs. Management reset its growth plan: FY27 volumes ~80 Mt (~8%), capacity target 119 Mt by end-FY27 (vs earlier 140-155 Mt), FY27 capex INR6,000-6,500 crore, and a cost reduction of about INR250/t in FY27 plus INR250/t in FY28. Pricing has not offset cost inflation, with April-over-March hikes of about INR10/bag in a few areas.

segments.name: Cement (consolidated)
segments.commentary: Capacity reached 109 Mt in FY26 after 10.7 Mt of new grinding and 7 Mt of clinker commissioning. Clinker capacity is 69 Mt, rising to 73 Mt with Maratha (4 Mt).

segments.name: Sanghi Industries
segments.commentary: Cement capacity utilization about 57%; management targets 65-70% for FY27. Turnaround is running behind schedule.

segments.name: Penna Cement
segments.commentary: Cement capacity utilization about 46%; management targets 55-60% for FY27. Management said maintenance needs and breakdowns were higher than expected.

segments.name: Orient Cement
segments.commentary: Management said Orient is operating at full capacity; Orient was consolidated for 11 months in FY26.

segments.name: Green power
segments.commentary: Green power share rose to about 32% in Q4 from 26% earlier; INR150-200/t savings are expected from fly ash and green energy.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated volume target of about 80 Mt, up about 8% from FY26; management described demand as soft, with industry growth of about 5-5.5%.
Cost reduction of about INR250/t on a full-year average in FY27 (target about INR4,250/t), with a further INR250/t reduction in FY28; Q1 FY27 cost expected flat at about INR4,500/t.
Capacity target lowered to about 119 Mt by end-FY27 from earlier 140-155 Mt; management said the FY28 capacity plan could slip by 1-2 years, to about FY30.
FY27 capex estimate of INR6,000-6,500 crore, with about INR4,000 crore already under execution; project IRR hurdle set at 18%.
Expected 10 Mt of capacity commissioning between now and September, including Salai Banwa and Warisaliganj; Mundra (2 Mt clinker) and Assam (2 Mt clinker) are planned for about 24-28 months out.
Management said it will not provide EBITDA/t guidance for now; the 15 Mt debottlenecking plan continues but timing may change.
capex_capacity: Capacity at 109 Mt; target 119 Mt by end-FY27 after about 10 Mt of ongoing additions including Salai Banwa and Warisaliganj.
Clinker capacity 69 Mt today; Maratha adds 4 Mt, and Mundra and Assam add 2 Mt each over about 24-28 months.

Management plans to shut some integrated-unit grinding capacity and move grinding closer to markets (North UP, Bihar, South Gujarat, Maharashtra); Bihar grinding to be set up, with Chhattisgarh becoming clinker-only.
Penna and Sanghi together hold 19 Mt of capacity; target is to raise their utilization by 5-10 points.
Efficiency capex (fly ash railway infrastructure and similar projects) is delayed by 3-6 months; benefits are expected from the coming quarters.
demand_pricing: Q4 demand was muted, with volume growth of about 10% in the investor deck; excluding Orient, management acknowledged volumes were roughly flat YoY in the March quarter.
Industry prices rose about INR10/bag in March quarter, with INR15-20 gains in select pockets; April demand was described as subdued.
Premium cement is about 36% of trade sales; the gap to base product is about INR50-55/bag for super premium and INR20-25/bag for premium.
Management said it would be happy with half of any industry price hike, given weak demand; price pass-through has not kept pace with cost.

qa_highlights.question: Volume growth is flattish ex-Orient in Q4, yet FY27 guidance implies about 8-10% growth on softer industry demand. What drives it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited stabilizing Sanghi and Penna plus about 10 Mt of new capacity commissioning between now and September 2026, which will be needed to reach 80 Mt.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cost outlook given the INR4,000/t exit target versus the reported INR4,500/t?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR4,000 was an aspiration for March exit; the March month was about INR4,100/t normalized, and INR4,500/t is the peak. A reduction of INR150-200/t is expected from fly ash and green energy, and INR250/t is the FY27 average target.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Ambuja's fixed cost rising faster than peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to higher branding (about INR70/t for FY26), repairs and maintenance at acquired assets, freight, lower government incentives and higher heat consumption. Acquired assets were said to drag EBITDA by about INR70-80/t.

qa_highlights.question: Is the reset of capacity and timelines a change in ambition?
qa_highlights.answer: Karan Adani said the target is not abandoned but the timeline has moved; capacity was stepped back to 119 Mt by end-FY27. Capital will be deployed only after current projects are completed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the 'core' versus 'non-core' working capital movement?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said core working capital fell from 30 to 20 days; non-core rose, partly from incentives accounted on an as-received basis, and some of the increase could be accounting-driven. ACC's negative operating cash flow reflects receivables from Ambuja under the MSA, which are to be settled via an ICD.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any EBITDA/t guidance or an IRR target for new capex?
qa_highlights.answer: No EBITDA/t guidance was given. Karan Adani said the project IRR hurdle is 18% on all-equity funding.

risks_watch: Acquired assets (Sanghi, Penna) remain well below target utilization and have had breakdowns; FY27 volume depends on them.
Q4 cost of about INR4,500/t was higher than guided; West Asia-related packing and fuel inflation of about INR250/t is an open risk, and Q1 FY27 cost is expected flat.
Price realization of about INR254/bag is flat QoQ, with limited pricing power in soft demand.
Capex has been delayed (Maratha, Chhattisgarh), and project timelines have been pushed out; the FY28 capacity plan may slip to FY30.
Working capital and non-core receivables rose sharply, and management said the non-core figure was partly accounting-driven; follow-up needed.
Sanghi railway (Naliya) and marine logistics timelines; 7 vessels to be delivered from next year.
Pending JP assets; management declined to comment as the seller is a listed company.
summary.management_tone: Candid and self-critical: management admitted under-delivery on cost, capex timelines and acquired-asset utilization, and reset guidance. Forward targets were framed as conditional on internal execution, with explicit caution on demand, pricing and fuel-cost volatility.

We are moving away from the time line.
It's capex -- I mean, the project IRR has to be 18%. this is all equity money.
